==Problem==
A certain calculator has only two keys [+1] and [x2]. When you press one of the keys, the calculator automatically  displays the result. For instance, if the calculator originally displayed "9" and you pressed [+1], it would display "10." If you then pressed [x2], it would display "20." Starting with the display "1," what is the fewest number of keystrokes you would need to reach "200"?

<math> \textbf{(A)}\ 8\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 9\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 10\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ 11\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 12</math>

==Solution 1 (Now rigorous)==
We can start at <imath>200</imath> and work our way down to <imath>1</imath>. We want to press the button that multiplies by <imath>2</imath> the most, but since we are going down instead of up, we divide by <imath>2</imath> instead. If we come across an odd number, then we will subtract that number by <imath>1</imath>. Notice
 <imath>200 \div 2 = 100</imath>,  
 <imath>100 \div 2 = 50</imath>,  
 <imath>50 \div 2 = 25</imath>,
 <imath>25-1 = 24</imath>,(Cannot divide by 2)  
 <imath>24 \div 2 = 12</imath>,  
 <imath>12 \div 2 = 6</imath>,  
 <imath>6 \div 2 = 3</imath>,  
 <imath>3-1 = 2</imath>,(Cannot divide by 2)   
 <imath>2 \div 2 = 1</imath>.   
Since we've reached <imath>1</imath>, it's clear that the answer should be <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 9}</imath>- <imath>\boxed{\textbf{Javapost}}</imath>. Because we only subtracted <imath>1</imath> when we had to, this is optimal. ~Roy2020 minor edits by IncredibleCheetah53

==Solution 2 (duodecimal)==
We make two key observations. First, pressing [x2] appends a <imath>0</imath> to the end of a number's binary representation. Second, pressing [x2] and then pressing [+1] appends to the end of a number's binary representation.

The base-ten number <imath>200</imath> is represented as <imath>11001000_2</imath> in binary. Therefore, the five <imath>0</imath>s contribute <imath>5</imath> button presses. Similarly, each of the three <imath>1</imath>s each contribute <imath>2</imath> button presses, although since we initially started with a <imath>1</imath> we can ignore one of the <imath>1</imath>s. Thus, the answer is <imath>5 + 2 \cdot 2 = \boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 9}</imath>.
